title: Your First Deployment
intro: A Deployment manages pods for you — if one dies, it gets replaced automatically. Let's create one.

steps.prompt: Create a deployment named 'web' using the nginx image with 3 replicas.
steps.explanation: Under the hood this creates a Deployment, which creates a ReplicaSet, which creates 3 Pods.

steps.fake_output:
NAME   READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE   AGE
web    3/3     3            3           10s
steps.explanation: READY 3/3 means all 3 desired replicas are up and healthy.

steps.prompt: See the actual pods it created.
steps.fake_output:
web-7d8f9c6b5-abcde   1/1   Running   0   10s
web-7d8f9c6b5-fghij   1/1   Running   0   10s
web-7d8f9c6b5-klmno   1/1   Running   0   10s
steps.explanation: Notice the pod names include a hash — that's the ReplicaSet's identifier, auto-generated.

steps.prompt: Delete one of the pods on purpose and see what happens (try 'kubectl delete pod web-7d8f9c6b5-abcde').
steps.fake_output:
pod "web-7d8f9c6b5-abcde" deleted

(a few seconds later)
web-7d8f9c6b5-pqrst   1/1   Running   0   2s
steps.explanation: This is the self-healing reconciliation loop in action — the Deployment noticed 2/3 pods and created a new one to get back to 3.
